purpose: Complete legacy GPU batch proving, GPU periodic setup and 32-chunk quotient commitments
result: Qualified on the selected NVIDIA laptop GPU; the broader GPU proving goal remains incomplete

fixtures: repeated three-transaction witnesses with fresh hiding
HTLC ordinary spend, redeem and refund
device_work: statement Poseidon folds and root chain
hiding, openings, FRI, transcript, grinding and scalar arithmetic
host_work: explicit CPU constraint audits in debug builds
admission: CPU-required and debug GPU-required requests reject before proving
oversized batches, private worker assignments and low host budgets reject before proof allocation
invalid join-split balance and HTLC mint reject
native empty/overflow counts, malformed policies and malformed host budgets preserve caller outputs
retired engines reject without CPU fallback
verification: unchanged CPU Rust and native batch verifiers accept after GPU shutdown
wrong roots, trailing proof bytes and damaged proof bytes reject
repeated witness batches receive fresh hiding
legacy_batch.wire_format: Unchanged postcard(Proof<config::MyConfig>) and 32-byte native root digest

unchanged_protocol_parameters: legacy security floor and maximum batch tile count

regressions.other: Candidate wallets, quotient/FRI, recursive sessions, worker admission and completion checks retained.

pilot_notes: Test-only statistics, constant and shape-field compilation errors were corrected before successful pilots.
An HTLC trace fixture initially enabled minting; it was corrected to vary fees while preserving the existing zero-mint rule.
The first complete batch attempt lacked a preprocessing receipt. GPU expansion now replaces CPU periodic-table replication, with bounded compact staging.
HTLC batch quotients exposed two commitment/storage count guards tied to LDE blowup. Both now use the existing 32-chunk compiler bound; heap byte limits and verifier parameters remain unchanged.
Opt-in component diagnostics are compiled only into fixture test binaries; production code does not log private component errors.

Pilot 06 verified all 24 Rust/native batch proofs in full/compact debug storage. Final qualification additionally checks compact periodic inputs and bounded trace diagnostics on the matching current source.

The first final qualification reached 96 checks and failed the quadratic/full quotient rejection fixture because it still classified 32 chunks as invalid. That failed run remains unchanged in run-01. The fixture now rejects 64 chunks.

The second final qualification also reached 96 checks, then failed the same test because its final counter expected four commitments instead of five. That failed run remains unchanged in run-02. The expected count and report now derive from the fixture array; run-03 uses fresh matching source and binaries.
limitations: Complete proof fixtures cover up to three transactions padded to four tiles; 64-tile trace/root assembly is verified, but complete 64-tile proving and capacity/throughput calibration remain unqualified.
C ABI GPU routing still requires existing Rust-side resident initialization in the same process; standalone native initialization/lifecycle remains open.
Private wallet worker admission, tree/recursive native delivery, quadratic lookup generation where required, owned multi-AIR commitments and full-size recursion remain open.
Default CPU selection is preserved; release GPU-required checks apply to the explicitly selected complete GPU path. Debug proof checks retain CPU constraint audits.
These correctness checks establish no sustained transaction-throughput or AMD/Metal result.
Pending Apple source still requires the authorized local Mac checkpoint commit; no SSH retrieval was attempted.
